───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ☐ Storage approach

│ How would you prefer to store and manage your data in your project? Consider factors like data persistence,
│ performance characteristics, ease of implementation, scalability requirements, and maintenance overhead. Which
│ approach best aligns with your project's needs and constraints?

❯ 1. In-Memory Storage
     Data stored entirely in application memory. Fast access and performance, but no persistence between restarts.
     Ideal for caching, temporary session data, or development/testing environments. Simple implementation with minimal
     overhead.
  2. File-Based Storage
     Persist data to files on disk in formats like JSON, CSV, or plain text. Offers a good balance between simplicity
     and data persistence. Suitable for small to medium datasets. Slower than in-memory but data survives restarts.
  3. Database
     Use a SQL or NoSQL database for data storage. Provides robust persistence, advanced querying capabilities,
     transaction support, and excellent scalability. More complex setup but handles large datasets and concurrent
     access reliably. Production-grade approach.
